subject.title: feat(ledger): add immutable action history core

question: Should ClawSweeper adopt this immutable JSONL ledger and its v1 identity, configuration, privacy, storage, replay, and CrabFleet projection contracts as the permanent action-history foundation?
rationale: The implementation can be correct while still creating durable product, operational, privacy, and compatibility commitments that automated review cannot authorize.

options.title: Adopt the v1 contract
options.body: Accept the complete architecture and explicitly own its long-term schema, configuration, privacy, retention, recovery, and projection obligations.

options.title: Narrow the first landing
options.body: Land only canonical identity and local immutable-storage primitives before committing to the complete import and external-projection contract.

options.title: Pause the ledger stack
options.body: Defer this PR and its dependent instrumentation until a different durable-history direction is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Adopt the v1 contract
recommendation.body: Accept the complete architecture and explicitly own its long-term schema, configuration, privacy, retention, recovery, and projection obligations.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main and adjacent repair history show the strongest ownership of ClawSweeper's central runtime and operational architecture.
